So deals are effectively already underway from mid-November, build through Thanksgiving week, peak on 27 November, and tail into Cyber Monday on 30 November.

runs.title: Pick the clearest TPS Supreme Court source
runs.prompt: The Trump administration has appealed to the Supreme Court to end Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Venezuelan migrants. Several outlets cover it. Visit each candidate and pick the one that best explains — in readable, non-paywalled text — what the administration is asking the Court to do and what happens to Venezuelan TPS holders meanwhile. Rank them and state which single source a normal reader should open first. Note any paywalls or bot walls you hit. Candidates: https://www.scotusblog.com/2026/11/trump-administration-asks-supreme-court-to-block-lower-court-ruling-keeping-protected-status-in-/ , https://thehill.com/regulation/court-battles/6228525-trump-urges-scotus-stop-venezuela-tps/ , https://www.riotimesonline.com/venezuela-tps-supreme-court-ninth-circuit-2026/ , https://www.firstpost.com/world/trump-administration-makes-third-supreme-court-appeal-to-end-tps-for-venezuelan-migr
runs.answer: Open SCOTUSblog first: it's the only candidate that loaded as full, free, readable text, and Amy Howe explains that Solicitor General D. John Sauer asked the justices to block Judge Edward Chen's September 2025 ruling keeping Venezuelan TPS in place, warning that otherwise the order "will spring into effect, inflicting severe and immediate harm" and that roughly 1,800 detained Venezuelans could be released; meanwhile the 9th Circuit's administrative stay kept Chen's ruling on hold (itself due to expire Nov 20), so TPS stayed terminated and removal could continue while the case proceeds. Importantly, the piece is updated to Nov 19: the administration withdrew the application a few hours after filing when the 9th Circuit extended its stay until seven days after it rules, and Sauer said he would return to the Court immediately if the 9th Circuit rules against the government — so a reader should know the "appeal" was pulled, not decided. Ranking: (1) SCOTUSblog, clear winner; (2) The Rio Times, which loads without a paywall but whose article text is buried under market tickers and megamenu navigation, leaving only its headline ("Supreme Court Voids Ruling Shielding Venezuelans in US")
